item.title: Hegseth has remained defiant as Congress members deliberate articles of impeachment
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is fighting back. As members of Congress begin deliberating on the articles of impeachment against him, Hegseth gave his first press conference in months.
item.content:encoded: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is fighting back. As members of Congress begin deliberating on the articles of impeachment against him, Hegseth gave his first press conference in months.

item.title: The scandal surrounding the head of Nvidia could have wide-ranging implications
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Bloomberg tech reporter Ian King about the unusually overarching role of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at his company and within the American tech industry at large.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Bloomberg tech reporter Ian King about the unusually overarching role of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at his company and within the American tech industry at large.

item.title: House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth
item.description: House Republicans managed to short-circuit a floor vote on the impeachment effort brought against the Defense Secretary by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.

item.title: Supreme Court seems split over federal agencies' ability to fine for law violations
item.description: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case related to temporary worker visas. The company involved says enforcement issues should go through the courts, not the federal agency alone.

item.title: What the U.S. midterms mean for Ukrainians heading into their 5th winter at war
item.description: Ukrainians are heading into their fifth winter at war. Russia has stepped up its bombing campaign of Ukraine's critical infrastructure. But Ukrainians see one bright spot — the U.S. midterm elections.

item.title: Democrats made gains in legislatures across the country
item.description: Democrats saw sweeping wins in state legislatures in the midterm elections — and it could bring changes in reproductive rights, health care and other issues.

item.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as their next leader
item.description: House GOP lawmakers have chosen Ohio's Jim Jordan to serve as minority leader, elevating a co-founder of the ultra-conservative Freedom Caucus to succeed Mike Johnson as the chamber's top Republican.

item.description: The so-called billionaire tax has failed in California. With proposition 40 dead, here's what could be next for future wealth taxes.

item.title: Russia's most famous independent newspaper has shut down after more than 30 years
item.description: Russia's top independent newspaper is closing after more than 30 years amid state pressure and censorship laws. Its founder won the Nobel Peace Prize and several of its journalists have been killed.

item.title: Tattoo artists are carrying Rembrandt's art into a new era — and a new medium
item.description: The Rembrandt House Museum in Amsterdam hosted an unusual exhibit in recent weeks — a renowned tattoo artist inking the Dutch master's designs on visitors' skin.
